title: Review and the Seen archive
spec: Marking a title watched asks for 1-5 stars (required) and an optional free-text review, stamps watched_at, sets status=seen and removes it from the queue without deleting it. The Seen archive is a BROWSABLE shelf, not a graveyard: cover art, stars, the date, the review, sortable by date watched and by rating, filterable by kind. Un-watching returns a title to the end of the queue and keeps the review. ACCEPT: rating a title moves it out of the queue and into Seen with its art intact; the archive is worth opening on its own.

locate.evidence: LOCATE: PATCH /api/titles/{id} (T-6) already takes a sparse body and was designed for exactly this — stars and review land there rather than in a new endpoint. The schema (T-2) already has status, stars with a CHECK BETWEEN 1 AND 5, review and watched_at; no migration. GET /api/titles?status=seen already filters (T-4) and the queue/wheel/wall all read status='queued' already, so AC3 is largely a consequence of setting status — but must be VERIFIED on all three rather than assumed. frontend/src/kinds.js (T-6) supplies the verb. The queue's filter-chip pattern (T-7) is reused for the archive. RISK: clearing queue_position to NULL means the list ordering 'queue_position IS NULL, queue_position, added_at' would sort seen rows first if they were ever included — the seen query must order by watched_at instead.

plan.evidence: PLAN: (1) extend PATCH to accept stars/review/status with validation and the queue_position clearing; (2) a star-rating control on the title page; (3) the archive view with sort and filter; (4) un-watch returning to the queue tail; (5) styles into base.css. DECISIONS: rating and un-rating both go through the existing sparse PATCH rather than new verbs, which is why T-6 built it sparse; un-watching appends at MAX+10 rather than restoring the old position, because the queue moved on while it was away and a resurrected stale position would be wrong; stars and review are deliberately NOT cleared on un-watch so a rewatch keeps the first opinion; and the archive sorts by watched_at DESC by default because the most recent thing you finished is what you want to see first.

build.evidence: BUILT AND PROVEN — .autodev/evidence/T-9/build.md. AC3 checked on ALL THREE surfaces as the spec demanded rather than the one in front of me: the rated game vanished from the queue (9 rows) and from the wheel (9 wedges) while total rows stayed 11, with status=seen, queue_position NULL and watched_at stamped. AC2: the game's button read 'Mark as played' and its line 'played 9/4/2026', read from kinds.js rather than re-decided. AC5 proven at both the API and through the UI button: status returns to queued at the END of the queue (position 120, the max), watched_at cleared, and stars 5 plus the review BOTH intact — a rewatch does not erase the first opinion. AC6: 0, 6, 'three', 3.5 and true all rejected with 400, and true specifically because Python's isinstance(True, int) is True so booleans needed an explicit guard; status=seen with no stars is also 400. auto-review.evidence: REVIEWED — no defect survived; one was prevented at locate rather than found at test. The seen listing would have inherited the queue's ORDER BY 'queue_position IS NULL, queue_position, added_at', which is meaningless for rows whose queue_position is NULL by definition — spotted while reading T-4's list handler and changed to watched_at DESC before it could ship. Decisions standing with reasons: rating and un-rating both go through T-6's sparse PATCH rather than new verbs, which is what that endpoint was built sparse FOR; picking a star is itself the action so there is no confirm button and therefore no half-finished state; un-watch appends at MAX+10 rather than restoring a stale position because the queue moved on while the title was away; stars and review are deliberately preserved through un-watch; and boolean stars are rejected explicitly because Python treats bools as ints and true would otherwise have passed the 1..5 range check.
